summary.headline: Yatra Q2 FY27 revenue fell 39% YoY to INR2,136 million and adjusted EBITDA fell 41% to INR150 million, while gross margin held flat at INR1,255 million.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was hit by a sharp MICE contraction (gross bookings down 63% YoY) and a weak travel backdrop from the West Asia conflict, higher fares and a weaker rupee. Core air gross bookings grew 15% YoY and air gross margin rose to 4.45% of bookings, with stand-alone hotels and corporate travel also growing. Other expenses rose by about INR13 crore, mainly affiliate commissions, which management says is a short-term measure. Net loss was INR7 million for the quarter and INR4 million for H1. Management is not giving formal guidance, but says MICE order book improved into Q3.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted EBITDA to gross margin ratio

financial_highlights.change: net cash up INR331 million QoQ

segments.name: Air ticketing
segments.commentary: Q2 gross bookings INR17,006 million (+15% YoY); gross margin INR757 million (+29% YoY); gross margin on bookings 4.45% vs 3.95%; passengers 1,298,000 (-2% YoY). H1 bookings INR33,585 million (+16%), margin 4.33% vs 4.26%.

segments.name: Hotels and packages (total)
segments.commentary: Q2 gross bookings INR4,054 million (-21% YoY); gross margin INR299 million (-34%); margin 7.37% vs 8.86%; room nights 490,000 (-3%). H1 bookings INR7,930 million (-8%), margin INR684 million (-11%), room nights 1,038,000 (+12%).

segments.name: Stand-alone hotels
segments.commentary: Gross bookings grew about 20% YoY in Q2, which management says is independent of MICE weakness.

segments.name: MICE
segments.commentary: Gross bookings down about 63% YoY on a very strong Q2 FY26 base; up about 37% QoQ. Margins under pressure as Yatra accepted lower pricing to rebuild volume.

segments.name: Corporate travel
segments.commentary: Gross bookings up about 18% YoY; about 54% of existing customers expanded spend; 177 new corporate customers went live during the year.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 guidance given; management reiterated the medium-term framework of about 15% gross booking growth translating into RLSC and EBITDA growth.
Management expects H2 to improve on H1, with MICE order book improving and air and hotels trending slightly better in Q3 and better in Q4.
Operating leverage: about 60% of the cost base is fixed; management says INR0.60 of each incremental rupee of income should flow to profit, on the current business mix.
Other expenses to taper by INR3-4 crore in coming quarters; normalised other expenses about INR47-48 crore per quarter.
Debt expected to improve materially in Q3 as IPO proceeds are used; full benefit seen in Q4.
Management indicated Q3 gross margin and RLSC growth in low to mid-teens for the full year, but did not confirm this.
capex_capacity: Kanoo partnership: Yatra manages about 30% of Kanoo's corporate business in the region; only about 1.5 months of execution in Q2, already contributing positively at the operating level.
Technology investments include GCP; AI assistant chats grew about 25% QoQ and cancellations via chat grew 67%.
Operating headcount efficiency improved about 5% YoY.
Approximately INR52 million of Q2 costs went into growth initiatives (GCP, Kanoo, RECAP, Travel Pro).
US Holdco restructuring is in progress across Cyprus, US, Singapore and Cayman; no completion timeline given for this financial year.
demand_pricing: Domestic air passenger traffic down about 6% YoY and about 15% QoQ; international traffic of Indian carriers down about 19% YoY; domestic fares up about 26% YoY and international fares up about 20%.
Yatra domestic air passengers were down 2.4% YoY but up about 4% QoQ, against an industry decline of nearly 15% QoQ.
Middle East is about 35-40% of international travel; still muted by about 15-20%. MICE and short-haul holidays are most affected.
MICE pricing was relaxed to rebuild volume, which compressed margins; management described this as a deliberate short-term choice.
Smaller agents are being squeezed by higher working capital needs; management says the same ticket cost INR2 lakh last year and INR3.5 lakh now.
Trade receivables rose to INR610 crore at Sept 2026 from INR535 crore at March 2026, mainly from corporate growth and airline receivables; management says DSO is unchanged for corporate.

qa_highlights.question: Why was gross margin only 2% higher QoQ despite MICE recovery and Kanoo revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said MICE was priced more flexibly to rebuild volume, so volume rose faster than margin. Kanoo has only about 1.5 months of execution, so Q2 is not yet representative.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about INR13-15 crore YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly affiliate commissions tied to higher affiliate-channel air volumes. Management said this is short-term; about INR3-4 crore should taper in coming quarters, with normalised other expenses about INR47-48 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company give margin guidance, and what is the operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal guidance. Management said margins should recover as volume returns, with about 60% of costs fixed, and a walk bridging gross margin to variable costs will be added to investor presentations.

qa_highlights.question: Why has debt increased and how will it trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower MICE advances reduced customer float. Unused IPO proceeds are being used to repay debt, with material improvement expected in Q3 and full benefit in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivables position and DSO trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Trade receivables rose to INR610 crore from INR535 crore at March 2026, mostly corporate and airline. Management said corporate DSO has not changed materially.

qa_highlights.question: Is air margin quality sustainable and how much is from affiliates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to air gross margin at 4.45% (vs 3.95%). Affiliate spend is mostly air but also includes hotels; stripping it out still shows about 20-25 bps YoY improvement from better negotiations.

risks_watch: MICE recovery depends on international group travel returning; Middle East exposure is still muted by about 15-20%.
Other expenses (affiliate commissions) are elevated and their taper is not yet visible.
Debt and working capital: rising trade receivables and higher debt despite IPO proceeds being deployed.
Corporate card partnerships with banks are delayed by the cost of credit, which limits the receivables offset.
US Holdco restructuring has no firm completion timeline.
Smaller agents being squeezed could benefit Yatra but also shows system-level stress in B2B demand.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core air, hotel and corporate franchise but cautious on near-term macro and MICE; management avoided formal guidance and was more evasive on the drivers of other expenses and debt, which it attributed to temporary factors.
key_quotes: So this is more of a strategic call that we took at this point of time to start at least building the volume back into the business and be a bit more aggressive on the pricing.
This would not be, Nitin, a permanent fixture where you would see other costs being -- other expenses being at these elevated levels.
On the operating leverage, approximately 60% of our cost is fixed in nature, right, which is basically salary costs, infrastructure costs, data center costs.
periods of disruption have often been when Yatra has done some of its most important building. This time is no different.

growth.why: No formal FY27 guidance; management only reiterated a medium-term framework of about 15% gross booking growth, with H2 improvement expected from a MICE order book and Kanoo/corporate wins but no specific capacity or contracted numbers behind it.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Adjusted EBITDA to gross margin at 11.96% in Q2 (H1 12.12%) and EBITDA margin around 10%; management expects other expenses to taper INR3-4 crore toward a normalised INR47-48 crore per quarter and ~60% of costs are fixed, but gives no formal margin guidance and MICE is being priced lower.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plants, lines, stores or fleet discussed; growth is from Kanoo partnership and corporate/stand-alone hotel wins, not added capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: H2 FY27 (Q3 slightly better, Q4 better)
rows.why: Gross bookings up 6% YoY to INR21,655 million in Q2 with air bookings +15% and MICE up ~37% QoQ; management expects Q3 air/hotels slightly better and Q4 better, and reiterates a ~15% medium-term booking growth framework, though Q2 bookings were not 15%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex or utilisation not discussed; asset-light model with net cash of INR2,180 million at 30 Sep 2026 and no capacity plan given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no formal FY27 guidance and only said Q3 gross margin and RLSC growth could be low-to-mid teens without confirming it, while Q2 revenue fell 39% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue down 39% YoY and H1 revenue down 28%, MICE bookings down ~63% YoY, Middle East still muting international demand by 15-20%, and affiliate commissions elevated with no visible taper yet.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launches were discussed; AI assistant and GCP technology investments are existing initiatives.

rows.label: Debt reduction from IPO proceeds
rows.when: Q3 FY27 material; full benefit Q4 FY27
rows.why: Unused IPO proceeds are being used to repay debt, with management expecting material improvement in Q3 and full benefit in Q4, against net cash of INR2,180 million at 30 Sep 2026.

rows.label: Trade receivables build-up
rows.why: Trade receivables rose to INR610 crore at Sept 2026 from INR535 crore at March 2026, and lower MICE advances cut customer float; corporate card partnerships are delayed by cost of credit.

rows.label: Kanoo corporate partnership ramp
rows.why: Yatra manages about 30% of Kanoo's regional corporate business with only ~1.5 months of execution in Q2, already contributing positively at operating level, so it should ramp over the next few quarters.
